About

Always eager to learn and tackle new challenges, I'm passionate about driving innovation in Robotics, Perception & Planning, seeking opportunities to apply my skills and contribute to cutting-edge projects that push the boundaries of technology.

I thrive in dynamic environments and am excited to wear multiple hats, leveraging both my technical and entrepreneurial skills. I’m strong-willed and determined—always searching for challenges, as comfort is boring to me. My growth is fueled by pushing boundaries and overcoming new obstacles.

Currently, I’m seeking a challenging full-time opportunity where I can apply my skills to advance the future of robotics. I thrive in fast-paced, innovation-driven environments and love tackling complex problems at the intersection of AI and real-world robotics.

When I'm not immersed in technical pursuits, I find joy in the art of singing. I frequently perform solo in front of live audiences.

Let's connect to discuss how we can innovate and build a future together! I'm open to networking, collaborations, and discussing exciting ventures in technology and beyond.

    Excited to share a recent fix I contributed to Xournal++!

    Xournal++ is an open-source app I use almost every day for note-taking and annotating PDFs. On Windows, creating a new file could sometimes suggest an empty filename if the default format included certain date/time codes (%F, %T, %V).
    I fixed this by making the filename generation Windows-compatible, so users now see proper suggestions like "2025-08-25-Note-15-30" instead of a blank box.

    A small tweak, but one that smooths out the user experience

    Students at conferences often feel intimidated approaching representatives from companies they're interested in because they believe they're asking for something. I was intimidated initially but then I realised that that we're not just asking but also bringing something to the table. Professionals are usually happy to provide guidance and engage with students because they've been in our shoes and understand the challenges of navigating the job market. Infact they appreciate our initiative and courage to approach them. I recently had a conversation about this with Martin Buehler, who was very encouraging and insightful. He emphasized that professionals are often eager to mentor students because they see us as the future workforce.

    In this rough job market, especially for new grads like me, it might seem like attending conferences is not worth the effort and won't lead to job opportunities. However, I believe in attending with the intention of gaining exposure to real-world robotics and networking with industry professionals whom I can learn from and build long-term connections with. I believe conferences are just the beginning of a rewarding journey in the industry!
